newsitem.title: USA: U.S. JUDGE ADJOURNS MASSACHUSETTS UPS HEARING.
newsitem.headline: U.S. JUDGE ADJOURNS MASSACHUSETTS UPS HEARING.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America Inc failed on Friday to win a restraining order against striking workers in a U.S. District Court in Boston.

U.S. District Court Judge George O'Toole adjourned until 1000 EDT/1400 GMT on Monday a hearing into the UPS motion seeking a restraining order against picketing workers at five company facilities in Massachusetts.
O'Toole ruled that for him to have jurisdiction in the case, the giant parcel delivery company must prove that strikers committed unlawful activities resulting in $75,000 in damages.

Lawyers for UPS alleged that strikers have inhibited customers from doing business and have prevented workers from delivering packages, and that UPS has had to hire extra security costing at least $15,000 a day at just one of the strike locations in Massachusetts since Sunday.

But lawyers for the Teamsters union objected that loss of business is a normal consequence of a strike and picketers have the right to block company truckers. Furthermore, alleged unlawful activities by strikers did not occur until a few days after the strike began, and therefore UPS was miscalculating the costs of extra security due to damages, the union charged.
"I think the best course is to permit the plaintiff a bit longer to answer the jurisdictional question," O'Toole told the court. "The matter is a central one."
